context.description: A fold, a live actor and a resumed actor reach the same snapshot

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review of packages/opencode/test/task/verify-spec-RM5.spec.ts (41 tests, my own run under load average 40: 41 pass, 0 fail, 10828 expect calls, 64 s). Given (40 seeded sequences of 100 random facts over release-notes, incl. after the end): 40 seed tests, mulberry32, each asserts exactly 100 facts on the plan from Blend.load; the sequence is never cut at the end; the summary test asserts all 18 FactSchema types occur (count pinned to FactSchema.members), unknown ids T7, T7.c1, S99 occur, at least 30 runs end inside their 100 facts and more than 200 facts arrive after an end, and every post-end fact returns the identical snapshot. When (fold with apply and send to a live actor of the same machine): the fold is engine.initial plus engine.apply per fact; the live actor is createActor(TaskMachine.machine(plan)), the memoised machine, started in Effect.scoped and sent every fact. And (prefix folded, restored, sent the rest): getPersistedSnapshot of the prefix fold, createActor(machine, {snapshot}), sent the suffix; at least 20 prefixes before the end and 5 after it. Then (three snapshots equal): status, value, full context including the log, and sorted tags are equal for fold vs live, restored vs fold and restored vs live on every seed; a control shows a restored actor that misses one moving fact differs, so the comparison has power. And (log grows exactly when the state or another context field changes): every step checks the old log is kept; any change of status, value or a non-log context field must append; a step with no change and no entry must return the identical snapshot; a growth with no other change is allowed only for run.started, run.resumed and spec.checked, as exactly one run entry with from === to. I judged that exception afresh: the spine prescribes these notes (AD-5 'a targetless row that writes context always appends an entry'; fact table 'run.resumed: run history entry resumed'), the machine's resume/begin/check actions write only that note, so the literal Gherkin contradicts the spine's own rule; the test asserts the strongest true form, names the exception in every seed title and bounds it tightly. The wording gap is already listed for the owner in journal/scenario-findings.md. It does not weaken the step's purpose (no silent change, no spurious entry).
